confirmed_facts.fact: Return was requested 3.9 days after delivery, inside the 7-day electronics window under Return v2; only one policy version applies.
Return parcel was picked up sealed at 0.82 kg and received at 0.81 kg; courier events are in order.
Warehouse photo shows serial WH900-72841 on the returned unit; the dispatch record lists WH900-78241. The two differ only by swapped characters at positions 8 and 9.
The dispatch serial was keyed in by hand and no dispatch scan exists.

findings.description: Dispatch serial WH900-78241 differs from the serial on the returned unit, WH900-72841. The seller believes a different unit was returned. The records do not show which serial was actually shipped.

evidence.quote: We believe a different unit was returned.

findings.description: No scan or photo confirms the dispatch serial, so a typing error at dispatch cannot be confirmed or ruled out. The photo shows the returned unit, not the shipped unit.

evidence.quote: Serial keyed in by hand: packing scanner offline

findings.description: The inspection notes the item appears used with worn earcup cushions but does not confirm or rule out the reported fault, and wear is a signal that needs explaining, not proof of cause.

policy_references.quote: same serial number as the dispatch record
Missing evidence is requested from the party that holds it (seller, courier, warehouse or customer). Never assume what it would show.

findings.rationale: The return is inside the window, but the returned serial differs from the dispatch serial and the dispatch serial has no scan. The seller holds the evidence that could settle which serial was shipped, so a draft request to the seller is saved (DRAFT-RET-2048-SELLER). No conclusion is drawn about who caused the difference.
findings.uncertainty_note: Whether the mismatch is a hand-keying error at dispatch or a different unit returned is unknown until the seller supplies evidence. The fault claim is also not confirmed by the inspection.
